Name: Theism
Description: The view that a personal or providential God (or gods) exists and is metaphysically fundamental to reality.

Name: Materialism / Naturalism / Physicalism
Description: The view that reality is ultimately physical or natural, without appeal to immaterial souls, forms, or supernatural causes.

Name: Nominalism / Anti-essentialism
Description: The view that general categories, universals, and essences are human constructs or labels rather than mind-independent realities.

Name: Platonism / Realism about Forms
Description: The view that abstract Forms, universals, or ideal realities exist independently of and more fundamentally than the physical world.

Name: Existentialist / Phenomenological Ontology
Description: Accounts of being grounded in lived experience, consciousness, and the concrete structures of existing in the world.

Name: Hindu / Daoist / East-South Asian Metaphysics
Description: Metaphysical frameworks from Hindu and Daoist traditions, including non-dualism, the Dao, and cosmic or processual views of reality.

Name: Moral Realism / Value Theory
Description: The view that moral or evaluative facts and values are objectively real features of the world.

Name: Idealism
Description: The view that reality is fundamentally mental or spiritual in nature, with matter dependent on or constituted by mind.

Name: Skepticism / Anti-metaphysics
Description: Doubt about the possibility of secure metaphysical knowledge, or rejection of traditional metaphysical questions as confused or meaningless.

Name: Dualism
Description: The view that reality (or the human person) is composed of two fundamentally distinct kinds of substance, typically mind and matter.

Name: Aristotelian Realism / Hylomorphism
Description: The Aristotelian view that things are composites of form and matter, with substances as the basic units of reality.

Name: Social / Political Metaphysics
Description: Accounts of reality centered on social structures, historical forces, or the material conditions of collective life.

Name: Pluralism
Description: The view that reality is composed of many distinct, irreducible kinds of things rather than one unified substance or principle.

Name: Buddhist Non-dualism / Emptiness
Description: The Buddhist view that phenomena lack fixed, independent essence (emptiness) and arise through dependent origination.

Name: Pantheism / Process Philosophy
Description: The view that God is identical with or immanent in nature, or that reality is best understood as ongoing process rather than fixed substance.
